articles.title: Vol 3 No. 10 Official Publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association OCT, 1991
articles.summary: This October 1991 newsletter from the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) details upcoming club activities including multiple star parties at various parks, general meetings, and board meetings, while also announcing a change in the Board of Directors and Ephemeris editor. It provides information on magazine subscriptions and highlights a special "Grand Tour of the Solar System" lecture by Andrew Fraknoi, Executive Director of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific, covering discoveries from recent space probes.

articles.title: CATCHING SOME RAYS IN THE SJAA
articles.summary: Jack Zeiders plans to build two white-light solar telescopes, one for the SJAA and one for Fremont Peak Observatory, utilizing a modified John Dobson design. Inspired by views at RTMC, he proposes that the SJAA also acquire a Hydrogen Alpha filter to enhance public solar viewing capabilities. He has researched various H-alpha filter options and has initiated a fundraising effort with a personal donation to purchase one for the club.

articles.title: LETTERS TO THE EDITOR
articles.summary: John Gleason, the outgoing editor of the "Ephemeris" newsletter, writes his 85th and final letter, expressing gratitude for his tenure and the opportunity to connect with club activities and contributors. He clarifies that his departure is not due to dissatisfaction or disinterest in amateur astronomy. The newsletter is likely associated with the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA).

articles.title: PERSEID METEORS AND A FIREBALL
articles.summary: Jeff Horne details his extensive preparations and multi-night observations of the Perseid meteor shower in early August. Despite challenges with equipment and weather, his observations culminated in an astonishing sighting of an intensely bright green, magnitude -8 fireball unrelated to the Perseids, which illuminated the landscape and left both observers stunned.

articles.title: DOUBLE, TRIPLE, AND MULTIPLE STARS
articles.summary: The article highlights that the autumn sky is rich in variable stars, with many of the most famous examples, such as Beta Lyrae, Delta Cephei, Mira, and Algol, also being components of complex multiple star systems. It describes the specific characteristics of these prototype variable stars, including their variability types, periods, and the number of physical and optical companions in their respective systems.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: ASTRO ADS is a free classifieds service for non-commercial advertisers to sell astronomy-related products or services. Ads must be submitted to the Editor by the 15th of each month to appear approximately three months later. The document also includes examples of classified ads for Telescope Eyepieces and Meade/Celestron equipment.

articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS - Page 5
articles.summary: This page from the SJAA Ephemeris features several classified advertisements for used astronomical equipment, primarily telescopes and accessories. Listings include a Celestron 8 and an Astro Physics Star 12ED refractor for sale, as well as requests from members looking to purchase a used 8-inch Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope. Each ad specifies the item, condition, price, and contact information for potential buyers or sellers.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: This article provides updates on cometary activity, announcing the recent recovery of Periodic Comet Arend (1991u) and encouraging observations of other visible comets. It includes detailed ephemerides for Periodic Comet Hartley 2 (1991t) and Periodic Comet Wirtanen (1991s), outlining their celestial coordinates and predicted magnitudes for observers from late September through early November.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP APPLICATION
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It outlines different membership tiers and their corresponding fees, including options for general membership, membership with Sky & Telescope subscription, and junior membership. The form also provides instructions for submission, either in person at a meeting or by mail to the treasurer, Jack Peterson.

articles.title: MAKE CHECKS PAYABLE TO "SJAA"
articles.summary: This document provides administrative information for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), including instructions for membership payment and renewal (New, Renewal, Junior, Membership only, Membership/S&T). It also announces a general meeting on October 19th at 8 PM and details for the monthly publication 'SJAA Ephemeris', encouraging member submissions by the 12th of the previous month.
